author: Literature Devil
description:
When does Batman’s mercy stop being heroic—and start becoming unethical?

Batman’s no-kill rule is one of the defining principles of the Dark Knight. But refusing to kill someone and actively choosing to **save** them aren’t necessarily the same thing. So what happens when Batman saves a villain like the Joker, knowing innocent people may die the next time he escapes?

In this Batman video essay, I examine the ethics of Batman’s mercy through The Joker, Jason Todd / Red Hood, Ra’s al Ghul, Batman Begins, Under the Red Hood, Batman: Cacophony, The Killing Joke, A Death in the Family, and more.

Should Batman save the Joker if the Joker is already dying? Was Nolan’s Batman justified when he told Ra’s al Ghul, “I won’t kill you, but I don’t have to save you”? Does Batman have a moral obligation to preserve every life—or can unlimited mercy eventually become injustice toward the innocent?

title: When Is Batman's Mercy Actually Unethical?
